title: Airtable Bearer header and token response lookalikes and non-values
summary: A client id and expires_in value, a scheme-only Bearer header, and a Bearer header or access_token member holding a placeholder, an environment reference, a template reference or a masked display.
rationale: A client id and an expiry in seconds are not the token, a scheme with no value has nothing to protect, a placeholder or reference stands in for a value kept elsewhere, and a masked display has no recoverable value. Protecting any of these would redact text a reader needs.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are identifiers, placeholders, references, masked text or non-secret outputs, not credential values. That a placeholder or reference is not a value is a project decision, not a Airtable statement.

sources.supports: The OAuth access tokens you receive should be passed with your API requests as a `Authorization: Bearer header`.
`access_token` | An opaque string. Can be used to make requests to the Airtable API on behalf of the user, and cannot be recovered if lost.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
